description: One bounded 5x5 block-tridiagonal line solve using block elimination and back-substitution.

input.encoding: [N, then N row records; each row is lower[5x5], diagonal[5x5], upper[5x5], rhs[5]]
input.boundary_blocks: lower block in row 0 and upper block in row N-1 are all zero
input.row_condition: diagonal[a,a] > sum(abs(diagonal[a,b]), b!=a) + sum(abs(lower[a,b])) + sum(abs(upper[a,b])) for every scalar row

contract.operation: solve one block-tridiagonal linear system with block size five
contract.method: block Thomas elimination; each modified diagonal block solves five upper-block right-hand sides and one solution right-hand side by 5x5 partial-pivot Gaussian elimination; recover the vector with block back-substitution
contract.scalar_result: sum((q+1)*x[q]) over the flattened solution, where q is zero-based block-row/component order
contract.complexity: O(N*5^3) arithmetic work and O(N*5^2) storage
contract.scope: one bounded block-line solve; no CFD coefficient construction, explicit residual, three-dimensional sweep schedule, or full BT time-step

output.definition: one-based position-weighted sum of all solved components

workspace.meaning: Fixed upper-factor, transformed right-hand side, and block work arrays for at most four 5-component rows.
